title: Hotels & Homestays
description: Hotels, guesthouses and homestays: finding a room, your booking, check-in and check-out, breakfast, the Wi-Fi, and asking for things for your room.

phrases.english: Do you have any rooms free?
phrases.registerNotes: Kosong means empty or free; the answer if there's nothing is Penuh (We're full).

phrases.english: Could I see the room first?
phrases.registerNotes: Quite normal at homestays and guesthouses, especially if you haven't booked. Dulu (first) also makes a request sound easy-going.

phrases.indonesian: Saya sudah pesan kamar atas nama Sam.
phrases.english: I have a booking under the name Sam.
phrases.registerNotes: Atas nama (in the name of) gives the name on any booking. If you booked through an app, add lewat aplikasi.
phrases.cultureNote: Reception will ask for your passport, often with Boleh pinjam paspornya? (May I borrow your passport?), to note or copy the details. That's normal.

phrases.registerNotes: Check-in and check-out are said as in English. Check-in is usually from two in the afternoon; if the room isn't ready, ask to leave your bag.
Usually jam dua belas siang (noon). To ask for a later one: Bisa late check-out?
Termasuk means included. Then ask Sarapannya jam berapa? (What time is breakfast?)
Password is the everyday word; kata sandi is the official one you may see written.

phrases.indonesian: AC di kamar saya tidak dingin.
phrases.english: The air conditioning in my room isn't cold.
phrases.registerNotes: AC is said a-se. If it won't come on at all, say AC-nya mati (it's dead) or rusak (broken).
phrases.audioHint: A se di kamar saya tidak dingin.

phrases.english: Can I leave my bag here?
phrases.registerNotes: Titip means leaving something in someone's care: luggage before check-in or after check-out. It's the same word as in titip salam (send my regards).
Lagi (another, more) works for anything: bantal lagi (another pillow), selimut lagi (another blanket).
Ada …? (Is there …?) works for anything you need: Ada handuk? Ada sabun?
phrases.cultureNote: Cheaper homestays may have cold water only, sometimes with a mandi: a tank of water (bak mandi) and a scoop to pour it over yourself. Don't climb into the tank; the water is for everyone.
